title: Shopping in Ouarzazate-Zagora-Tinghir
supports: Tamegroute's pottery tradition and workshops as a visitor experience
hidden_gem_rationale: A hands-on craft stop in a small Drâa Valley village, distinct from Morocco's famous medinas and the established desert-camp circuit.

title: On course for a greener Morocco
supports: oyster farming in Oualidia lagoon and tasting oysters directly from local producers beside the lagoon
hidden_gem_rationale: A place-specific food experience tied to small lagoon producers, away from the country's heavily visited imperial-city and souk attractions.

title: Museums and art galleries in Morocco
supports: National Museum of Ceramics in Safi and its collection of Moroccan archaeological and ethnographic pottery
hidden_gem_rationale: A specialist national collection in a working ceramics city that is culturally substantial but absent from Morocco's standard palace-and-medina highlights.

title: Beach in Dakhla
supports: Punta Sarga as a southern-peninsula viewpoint over habitat for migratory birds, flamingos, turtles, rays and humpback dolphins
hidden_gem_rationale: A defined wildlife lookout at the far end of Dakhla's peninsula, secondary to the destination's famous kitesurfing and White Dune experiences.

title: Park Fees & Tariffs
supports: Kitulo National Park's Mbeya/Njombe location and status as Africa's first botanical national park, known as the Serengeti of Flowers
hidden_gem_rationale: A highland botanical walk in a little-visited park that offers a distinct experience beyond Tanzania's internationally famous wildlife circuits.

title: Rubondo Island National Park
supports: boat excursions around Rubondo, forested shores, beaches and possible sightings of waterbirds, crocodiles, hippos and otters
hidden_gem_rationale: A remote Lake Victoria island circuit with a park-defined boat experience, far less prominent than Tanzania's northern safari and Zanzibar routes.

title: Park Fees & Tariffs
supports: Mkomazi National Park's Kilimanjaro/Tanga location, black rhino sanctuary and African wild dog breeding programme
hidden_gem_rationale: A conservation-focused park visit near Same that is overshadowed by nearby Kilimanjaro and Tanzania's headline safari parks.

title: Semuliki National Park
supports: Sempaya's boiling geothermal springs inside East Africa's only true lowland tropical rainforest and access from the park gate
hidden_gem_rationale: A specific geothermal forest walk in one of Uganda's least visited national parks, distinct from the country's famous gorilla and savannah experiences.

title: Toro Semliki Wildlife Reserve
supports: seven-kilometre hike from reserve headquarters through savannah, woodland and gorge forest, with notable birds and possible primates
hidden_gem_rationale: A named ranger route within a reserve usually passed over for nearby Semuliki National Park, with a distinct habitat transition and strong birding value.

place: Khama Rhino Sanctuary guided game drive
title: Khama Rhino Sanctuary
supports: community management near Serowe, black and white rhino conservation and guided game drives
hidden_gem_rationale: A community-run conservation stop with a specific guided activity, outside Botswana's famous Okavango-Chobe safari axis.

title: Nxai Pan National Park – Nata Sanctuary
supports: Nata Bird Sanctuary as Botswana's first community-based conservation project, managed by four villages with tourism proceeds supporting local development
hidden_gem_rationale: A community-managed pan-edge sanctuary that offers a locally beneficial birding stop beyond Botswana's marquee national parks.

publisher: Moremi-Manonnye Conservation Trust and Botswana Tourism Organisation
title: Goo-Moremi Gorge
supports: community-managed conservation area in the Tswapong Hills, perennial streams, waterfalls, pools and hill hiking
hidden_gem_rationale: A defined community-run waterfall hike in Botswana's seldom-visited eastern hills, far from the country's dominant delta and big-game itinerary.

publisher: Namibia Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
title: Popa Falls Game Park
supports: small riverine park, four-metre Okavango rapids, walking and birdwatching, and more than 400 recorded bird species
hidden_gem_rationale: A compact river-and-birding stop usually used only as a gateway to larger northeastern parks, with a specific walkable landscape of its own.

publisher: Namibia Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
title: Nkasa Rupara National Park
supports: Namibia's largest protected wetland, buffalo concentration, two designated camps, 4WD recovery equipment and self-sufficiency requirements
hidden_gem_rationale: A demanding wetland wilderness camp in a little-visited park, offering a markedly different Namibia experience from Etosha and the Namib dunes.

publisher: Namibia Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
title: Namib-Naukluft Park
supports: Naukluft mountain section, Hartmann's mountain zebra sanctuary role and availability of hiking and walking trails
hidden_gem_rationale: A mountainous hiking experience within a park overwhelmingly associated with Sossusvlei, providing a separate landscape and activity from its famous dunes.

publisher: Namibia Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
title: Khaudum National Park
supports: deep Kalahari sand tracks, low visitor numbers, elephants and wild dogs, two-vehicle 4WD recommendation and food and water guidance
hidden_gem_rationale: A genuinely remote self-drive traverse with fewer than 3,000 annual visitors, supported by explicit park guidance and clearly distinct from Namibia's mainstream routes.
